answer_to_user:
Apples-to-apples answer: no, Toyota is NOT just cheap because of the yen — the valuation multiples are computed on a currency-consistent basis (every company shown in USD, and P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA are ratios so they are currency-neutral anyway), and against the German automakers Toyota actually looks the LEAST cheap of the mainstream group.

Current multiples (all USD, as-of 2026-06-30):
- Toyota (7203.JP): P/E 8.6 · P/B 0.96 · EV/EBITDA 8.0 · div yield 3.1%
- Volkswagen (VOW3.XETRA): P/E 7.0 · P/B 0.19 · EV/EBITDA 3.7 · div yield 7.2%
- Mercedes-Benz (MBG.XETRA): P/E 8.5 · P/B 0.47 · EV/EBITDA 8.3 · div yield 7.8%
- BMW (BMW.XETRA): P/E 5.6 · P/B 0.36 · EV/EBITDA 5.6 · div yield 7.6%
- Porsche AG (P911.XETRA): P/E 47.8 · P/B 1.75 · EV/EBITDA 6.6 · div yield 2.3%

So on a like-for-like basis BMW and Volkswagen are the cheapest (BMW ~5.6x earnings and 5.6x EV/EBITDA; VW an extraordinarily low 0.19x book and 3.7x EV/EBITDA — a distressed-looking multiple). Toyota (8.6x P/E, ~1.0x book, 8.0x EV/EBITDA) trades roughly in line with Mercedes and RICHER than BMW/VW — the yen optics were masking that it is the quality name of the group, not the cheapest. Porsche AG is the clear outlier on the expensive side (47.8x earnings). One nuance: Toyota carries a 12% ROE here vs the German names, so its premium to BMW/VW is partly a quality premium, not pure mispricing.
